text:
Sahana Iyer: working on the golden image pipeline hooks + rollback automation. can we align on *when* we auto-rollback candidate->stable, and how to avoid flip-flopping (candidate/stable toggles) during noisy validation?

Vanessa Ortiz: +1. we need something deterministic for operators + safe by default. last thing we want is a bad image thrashing every pool.

Harish Reddy: ops POV: if we auto-rollback too aggressively, we’ll bounce between versions all night. if we’re too conservative, we keep burning time-to-ready.

Keiko Yamamoto: what are we using as rollback signal? validation failure rate spike? time-to-ready regression? or specific “hard fail” checks (driver mismatch, kubelet join)?

Sahana Iyer: thinking of 2 buckets:
1) hard failures -> immediate rollback (or block promotion)
2) soft degradation -> rollback if sustained over window

Miles Thornton: pls tie to SLO burn-rate style thresholds rather than a single bad batch. otherwise one flaky NCCL run will roll back the world.

Nina Petrova: agree. also distinguish *image issues* vs *fleet issues*. NCCL smoke test can fail due to fabric, not image. if we rollback on that, we’re masking the real incident.

Fiona McCarthy: from SecOps: rollback needs audit trail + “no auto-promotion” if the candidate contains pending CVE exceptions. also prefer “rollback only within same hardened baseline” (don’t regress kernel hardening flags).

Vanessa Ortiz: can we define:
- candidate image is pinned per pool (image_channel=candidate + image_version)
- stable is last known-good for that pool type
- auto-rollback only flips channel pointer back to stable; doesn’t mutate stable itself

Sahana Iyer: yes. stable stays immutable, only updated via promotion step.

Jamal Pierce: for preventing flip-flop: add hysteresis + cooldown. e.g. if we rollback, don’t allow re-promote for X hours unless manual override.

Connor O'Brien: release angle: +1 cooldown + explicit “go/no-go” for re-promote during rollout week. we can wire it to the feature flag so rollback also disables rollout.

Benji Okafor: control plane can store “rollback lockout_until” per pool. readiness svc can enforce it when image_channel changes. also emit audit event (ties into the audit PR).

Keiko Yamamoto: proposing concrete policy:
- Hard fail triggers (immediate rollback / quarantine candidate):
  - driver/toolkit parity failure (nvidia-smi driver version != expected)
  - kubelet never joins within join timeout (but only if cluster healthy?)
  - node validation agent can’t start (daemonset missing / cert issues)
- Soft triggers (sustained, windowed):
  - post-provision validation failure rate > 5% over 30m AND at least 40 nodes attempted
  - time-to-ready P95 regression > 25% vs trailing 24h baseline for same region+gpu

Miles Thornton: close. we should avoid baseline comparisons during early rollout (baseline is unstable). use “stable image control group” in same pool type if we can.

Sahana Iyer: we can do: compare candidate cohort vs stable cohort in same region/gpu over same window. if candidate failure rate > (stable + 3%) OR >2x stable, trigger rollback.

Harish Reddy: love it. also set min sample size so we don’t rollback on 2 nodes.

Vanessa Ortiz: what about “flip-flop prevention” specifics?
- cooldown: 6h after auto-rollback
- require 2 consecutive green windows to re-promote (e.g. 60m each)
- manual override requires #eng-infra + release signoff

Connor O'Brien: works. add “one-way door” during rollout: if rollback triggers, we auto-disable the staged rollout flag for that region/gpu. re-enable requires oncall ack.

Fiona McCarthy: and ensure we log: who/what changed channel, prior version, new version, reason (metric + threshold). for compliance, please don’t store node IDs in audit payload.

Benji Okafor: ack, will keep audit event at pool-level (pool_id, region, gpu_type, old_channel/version, new_channel/version, reason_code). no per-node.

Nina Petrova: one more: avoid rollback on infra-wide incidents (network brownout). add a “global incident guardrail”: if cluster error rate is elevated across *stable* cohorts too, do not rollback candidate automatically.

Miles Thornton: +1. if stable is also failing at similar rate, rollback won’t help. use a condition like “stable failure rate < 2%” for candidate rollback to be eligible.

Sahana Iyer: summarizing proposal (plz react):
- Auto-rollback eligibility: stable cohort healthy (stable failures <2% and time-to-ready within +10% of 24h median)
- Hard fail: parity mismatch / validation agent not running -> block promotion + rollback if already rolling
- Soft fail: candidate vs stable delta thresholds with min sample size
- Flip-flop prevention:
  - rollback sets lockout_until = now+6h
  - require 2 green windows (>=40 nodes each) before allowing re-promote
  - auto-rollback also disables staged rollout flag for that slice

Vanessa Ortiz: :thumbsup: + add doc in golden image confluence + link in runbook.

Harish Reddy: :thumbsup: can we set cooldown to 12h for weekends? (less coverage)

Connor O'Brien: we can make it config by “coverage tier”. default 6h weekdays, 12h weekends.

Keiko Yamamoto: :thumbsup: please write down the exact metrics names / tags so we implement consistently (region, gpu_type, pool_id, image_version). avoid adding node.

Sahana Iyer: yep. I’ll draft a short spec + add to ENG-4826 notes. also will add a config snippet for the orchestrator:
```
rollback:
  enabled: true
  cooldown_hours: 6
  min_sample_size: 40
  hard_fail_reasons:
    - DRIVER_PARITY_MISMATCH
    - VALIDATION_AGENT_START_FAILURE
  soft_fail:
    candidate_vs_stable_failure_rate_delta: 0.03
    candidate_vs_stable_failure_rate_ratio: 2.0
    window_minutes: 30
  guardrails:
    stable_failure_rate_max: 0.02
```

Fiona McCarthy: looks good. ping me on the audit event schema review.

Benji Okafor: will take the lockout_until + reason_code fields. should be small migration.

Vanessa Ortiz: ok let’s do it. Sahana can you also add “no auto rollback if operator sets override=true for active incident mitigation”? (we sometimes intentionally keep candidate for debugging)

Sahana Iyer: good call. adding `operator_override=true` disables auto rollback but still blocks promotion unless override reason set.

Miles Thornton: make sure override requires a reason string so we can postmortem.

Sahana Iyer: done. I’ll post the draft in #eng-infra tomorrow + wire the metrics comparisons once we have stable/control cohorts in dashboards.
